fields.label: Function Script
fields.description: Write your Python function here. Must include a main(context) function that returns a string value.

fields.label: Function Guidelines
fields.options:
Function Script Guidelines

Basic Structure:

def main(context):
    # Your code here
    return "your result"

Available Context Variables:

context = {
    'message': {
        'content': 'message content',
        'type': 'message type',
        'from': 'sender number'
    },
    'doc': frappe.get_doc('your target doctype'),
    'target_field': 'field being processed',
    'command': 'current command'
}

Example Use Cases:

1. Simple Value Processing:

def main(context):
    # Convert incoming message to uppercase
    return context['message']['content'].upper()

2. Database Interaction:

def main(context):
    # Fetch customer details
    customer = frappe.get_doc('Customer', 
        {'mobile_no': context['message']['from']})
    return f"Hello {customer.customer_name}!"

3. Conditional Logic:

def main(context):
    message = context['message']['content'].lower()
    if 'urgent' in message:
        return 'high'
    else:
        return 'normal'

Available Frappe Functions:

  • frappe.get_doc(doctype, name)
  • frappe.get_value(doctype, name, fieldname)
  • frappe.get_all(doctype, filters={}, fields=[])
  • frappe.format_date(date)
  • frappe.throw(msg)

Best Practices:

  • Always define a main(context) function
  • Handle exceptions appropriately
  • Keep functions focused and single-purpose
  • Add comments for complex logic
  • Return string values that can be stored in the target field
